# moddotplot-rs v0.5.0

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.5.0 completes the agreed scheduler and scientific-validation stage and adds
reproducible export. It remains a functional preview; additional usability work will
precede v1.0.0.

## Display-aware refinement

Scheduler policy 2 replaces fixed nomination bands with compact per-preview-tile
identity and direction-support histograms evaluated against the active heatmap floor.
It also selects immediate neighbors and a deterministic exploratory sample, preventing
weak or blank preview regions from becoming permanent refinement exclusions.

Preview remains optimized for rapid first structure. The scientific configurations
are unchanged: 256 registers for preview, 1,024 for detail, HLL p10, verified-winner
OPH, and sparse correction disabled. Scheduler policy is separately versioned because
it chooses work without changing either tier's numeric result.

The retained selective-mosaic characterization refines 63 of 108 tiles, 58.3% of
all-detail work, while meeting its coherence, error, display-floor, and last-visible-
change gates.

## Scientific evidence

The preregistered report compares production estimates with complete distinct
canonical k-mer-set containment after transforming both to displayed
`ANI_c=C^(1/k)`. This is an estimator test, not a claim that `ANI_c` is biological ANI
or alignment-derived `ANI_m`.

Across four deterministic hash layouts and the expanded fixture grid, mean/P95
absolute `ANI_c` errors were 0.035283/0.226630 for 256 registers and
0.005333/0.017890 for 1,024 registers. Combined 0.80-floor crossing rates were 2.8604%
and 1.1987%. Both production tiers pass their preregistered limits without sparse
correction. No verified-winner fingerprint collision was observed, and the expected
rates were too small to justify wider-fingerprint benchmarking in this release.

See the [scientific validation record](v0.5.0/SCIENTIFIC_VALIDATION.md) and retained
[machine-readable grid](v0.5.0/scientific-grid.tsv).

## Reproducible export and goldens

**Export data** writes exact fixed-point numeric renderer inputs for the current
viewport as CSV. **Export image** re-renders the current plot at twice its backing
resolution, bounded to eight million pixels, and writes PNG. CSV construction is
rejected above two million participating renderer cells. Both formats include complete
software, method, scheduler, comparison, scientific-configuration, display, viewport,
and sequence provenance; PNG stores it in a standards-compliant `iTXt` chunk.

The existing schema-1 numeric-channel golden remains byte-identical to v0.2.1. A stable
CPU golden now also fixes the similarity shader's representative RGBA transfer output.

See the [complete validation record](v0.5.0/VALIDATION.md) for release qualification.
